guardrails.titulo: Liveness and readiness probes defined
guardrails.verificacao: kubectl get deploy -o yaml | check livenessProbe and readinessProbe on every container; readiness should point to an endpoint that reflects real readiness

guardrails.titulo: CPU/memory requests and limits defined
guardrails.verificacao: kubectl get deploy -o yaml | check resources.requests and resources.limits on every container; values justified, not copy-pasted from an example

guardrails.titulo: Image without :latest, with a reproducible tag
guardrails.verificacao: grep -rn 'image:' k8s/ | no reference to :latest or missing tag; the tag must allow rebuilding the same image

guardrails.titulo: Configuration via ConfigMap/Secret, not hardcoded
guardrails.verificacao: kubectl get deploy -o yaml | sensitive or environment config comes from configMapKeyRef/secretKeyRef/envFrom; no fixed configuration value in the manifest or the image

guardrails.titulo: Service selector matches the Deployment's labels
guardrails.verificacao: kubectl get endpoints <svc> | non-empty endpoint list; compare the Service's spec.selector with the Deployment's template.metadata.labels

guardrails.titulo: Replicas >= 2 when the statement asks for resilience
guardrails.verificacao: kubectl get deploy | READY shows 2/2 or more; kubectl delete pod on one of them and confirm the service keeps responding and the pod gets recreated

guardrails.titulo: External call with timeout and retry with backoff
guardrails.verificacao: locate every network call in the code: does it have an explicit timeout? Limited retry with growing wait between attempts? Does the final failure become a handled error, not an uncaught exception?

guardrails.titulo: Input validated at the boundary
guardrails.verificacao: send a request with a missing, empty and malformed parameter: the response is a clear error (4xx) before any processing, with no stack trace leaking

guardrails.titulo: No secret in versioned code or manifest
guardrails.verificacao: grep -rniE 'password|secret|token|api_key' in the code and manifests | no literal credential; secrets come from env/Secret

guardrails.titulo: Minimal, justified dependencies
guardrails.verificacao: open the dependency manifest (package.json/requirements.txt): is every entry actually used? Could any of them be solved with the standard library in a few lines?

guardrails.titulo: Logs at the right level, no forgotten debug output
guardrails.verificacao: grep -rn 'print\|console.log' in the code | no debug printf outside the logger; errors log at error level with context, normal flow at info

guardrails.titulo: Error codes mapped (400/404/5xx distinct)
guardrails.verificacao: curl with invalid input → 400; nonexistent resource → 404; simulated internal failure → 5xx; the three cases return distinct codes and bodies

guardrails.titulo: Healthcheck without a heavy dependency
guardrails.verificacao: read the /healthz handler: does it respond fast without calling an external service or running an expensive query — otherwise the probe takes down a healthy pod whenever the dependency hiccups

guardrails.titulo: API contract documented
guardrails.verificacao: README or OpenAPI lists every route with method, parameters, example response and error codes; confirm it matches the real behavior via curl

guardrails.titulo: Cache with TTL and clear invalidation
guardrails.verificacao: when there is a cache: where is the TTL configured? What happens when it expires? Is there a way to force-refresh a stale entry? Test two consecutive requests and one after the TTL

guardrails.titulo: Tests cover the error case, not just the happy path
guardrails.verificacao: list the tests: is there at least one per relevant failure behavior (invalid input, nonexistent resource, dependency down)?

guardrails.titulo: A test would fail if the code broke
guardrails.verificacao: deliberately break a line of the code under test and run the suite: at least one test turns red; a test that compares the mock to itself doesn't count

guardrails.titulo: Offline fixture for external dependency
guardrails.verificacao: turn off the network (or point to a nonexistent host) and run the suite: it still passes, using a local fixture/recording instead of the real service

guardrails.titulo: The suite runs with one documented command
guardrails.verificacao: follow the README to the letter on a clean clone: a single command runs all the tests and exits with the correct status code

guardrails.titulo: Rollback documented
guardrails.verificacao: the README says how to go back to the previous version (e.g. kubectl rollout undo) and the command was run at least once to prove it works

guardrails.titulo: No orphaned resources left behind
guardrails.verificacao: kubectl get all and docker images | no abandoned test pod/deployment/image; anything not part of the deliverable was removed

guardrails.titulo: Reproducible step by step from scratch
guardrails.verificacao: follow the README on a clean environment (or mentally simulate each command): the sequence brings everything up from scratch with no implicit step, in the order written
